summary: Seal active at all times, Judgement on cooldown, Holy Shield kept up for block mitigation and threat, Consecration rolling (the AoE/multi-target backbone), Avenger's Shield on pulls. There is NO 969 rotation in TBC - that's a WotLK construct. Threat is seal + Judgement + Holy Shield + Consecration + melee.

Hammer of the Righteous.note: does NOT exist in TBC Classic (WotLK ability) - the most common wrong-expansion mistake for prot paladins; log is mislabeled

Divine Storm.note: does NOT exist in TBC Classic (WotLK Ret ability)

Crusader Strike.note: Retribution ability - wrong spec for a tank

Seal of Command.note: Retribution seal - a tank should run Seal of Righteousness/Vengeance for threat

Seal of Blood.note: Retribution seal (self-damage for AP) - wrong spec for a tank

Holy Light.note: Holy spec heal - a Prot paladin healing heavily is wrong spec or an emergency

Holy Shock.note: Holy spec ability - wrong spec for a tank

breakpoint.note: Holy Shield should be one of the HIGHEST cast counts and held at very high uptime - it's both the block wall and a major threat source; gaps are the single biggest mitigation/threat loss (usually mana-starvation or forgetting to refresh). Judgement on cooldown, Consecration rolling for sustained AoE threat, and the active seal should show near-constant uptime via melee swings.

advisory: TBC AoE/multi-target tank. Blessing of Sanctuary should be active (mitigation buff). Avenger's Shield is mainly a pull / ranged-threat opener (longish cooldown), not a filler. A tank casting Divine Shield (bubble) mid-fight drops all aggro - heavy mid-pull use is a red flag. Hammer of the Righteous does NOT exist in TBC, so do not expect it - its presence means the log is wrong-expansion. The mana budget caps how much Holy Shield + Consecration you can sustain, so prioritization matters.
